description: Canonical registry of conformance vector identifiers. Every ak.vector.* identifier referenced by prose or fixtures MUST appear here, and every row MUST point at the prose or fixture source that defines it.

vectors.description: Account Authority issuer ledger: genesis and CAS successor chaining, record identity and proof binding, the closed replica classification table, idempotency conflict and the bounded fanout outbox transitions.
Agent provisioning declares its principal-control Realm id forward, before the Agent PCR genesis Event is submitted.
Two signature-valid but different Commits on one (realm_id, stream_ref, authority_generation, stream_position) freeze that stream; consumers MUST NOT pick a winner.
Realm, Circle and Sidecar streams each start and advance their own predecessor chain; planned handoff transfers every private head without exposing hidden stream existence in the public bundle.
After a planned handoff is accepted, a write signed by the old generation is rejected; only the new generation extends the stream from the imported final head.
A RealmCommit whose predecessor leaves its own stream, skips a position, or nulls a non-zero position is rejected and writes nothing.

Minimal encrypted-envelope wire digest over RFC 8785 JCS {version,content_type,encryption_context} followed by decoded ciphertext bytes. Scope, Event kind, group id, scheme and sender domain are reconstructed inputs and never duplicated in the envelope.
ECDSA P-256 (ES256, RFC 6979 deterministic) detached JWS golden vector over the canonical proof binding object, mirroring the ed25519 vector structure for the optional interop signature suite.

ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) raw detached signature golden vector over the canonical proof binding object bytes (registry proof_kind raw_detached_signature; keygen from a recorded xi seed, signature published as a recorded value that verifiers only verify).
BLAKE3 KAT over fixed UTF-8 bytes plus wrong-prefix, wrong-length, Realm-suite mismatch, and unknown-suite downgrade rejection cases.
Suite-tagged Event ID derivation: the 33-octet body, its base64url token, and the negative cases for suite code, reserved nibble, padding and decoded length.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_p256_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM, profile-gated interop suite): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_x25519_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / ChaCha20-Poly1305): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.
Byte-exact recovery signing transcripts for every registered recovery factor; the verifier rebuilds the bytes from stored session state and the submitted proof.
Byte-level KAT for MLS ciphersuite 0x0001. The in-tree fixture pins the MLS WG corpus commit, every source-file SHA-256 digest, the ciphersuite selector, and fail-closed runner behavior.

Byte-exact Ed25519 KAT for the seven-field ak.franking_proof.signature.v1 transcript. The fixture removes only payload.signature, prepends the registered domain field, and rejects mutation of every bound member.
An event-derived object id is the retype of its own genesis Event token, byte for byte.
realm_id is the retype of its ak.realm.create Event token; a carried or non-derived value is rejected with realm_id_not_event_derived.
Own-Station account aggregate stream: per-stream tail continuity, durable cursor checkpoints, projection-before-checkpoint ordering, reconnect reset vs resume, and explicit delivery cancellation.
